content: This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as propylene glycol in the suspension, which can potentially cause allergic reactions or other complications. Fosamprenavir has the potential to elevate cholesterol and triglyceride levels in the blood. HIV infection itself can also contribute to this effect, which may increase the risk of cardiovascular issues, including heart attacks. It is essential to discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, as well as strategies to reduce your risk of heart disease. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary. Treatment with fosamprenavir can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and it may be included as part of the treatment regimen. However, it is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of severe side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. It is important to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of fosamprenavir from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, etravirine, and rifampin. Fosamprenavir itself can also influence the removal of other medications from your body, which may impact their effectiveness. This medication may reduce the efficacy of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to unintended pregnancy. Consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine whether you should use additional reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests should be conducted to monitor your health. These tests may include viral load, T-cell counts, liver function tests, cholesterol and triglyceride levels, and blood sugar levels. It is crucial to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than four hours since the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The suspension can be stored at room temperature or in the refrigerator. Refrigeration may improve the taste of the suspension, but do not freeze it. Avoid storing this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Fosamprenavir, commonly sold under the brand name Lexiva, is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, allowing the immune system to function more effectively. Fosamprenavir belongs to a class of drugs known as protease inhibitors. It may be administered with ritonavir, another protease inhibitor, to enhance (boost) its levels in the body. However, fosamprenavir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. If you are taking fosamprenavir suspension, shake the bottle well before each dose. Measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. Do not use a household spoon, as it may not provide the correct dose. Adults should take the suspension without food, while children should take it with food. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, other medications you may be taking, and whether you have previously used protease inhibitors to treat HIV. For children, the dosage is also based on age and weight. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, and do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed. Do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) even for a short time unless directed to do so by your doctor. Common side effects of fosamprenavir include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and headache. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or many months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Fosamprenavir commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking fosamprenavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to amprenavir, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as propylene glycol in the suspension, which can cause allergic reactions or other problems.
